email.subject: Send in your receipts by 31 December

body.v: Receipts for this year can only be refunded if you upload them by 31 December.
Upload them in the HelvetiCare app, under Claims. It takes a few minutes.
We never ask for receipts or bank details by email.

hotspots.explain: The address is on helveticare.example, the insurer's real domain.
A real deadline, but nothing is hidden: it says what, where and by when. Urgency alone does not make an email a scam.
It tells you to use the app, not a link.
It says clearly that it never asks for receipts or bank details by email.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: HelvetiCare: the address is on helveticare.example.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Some urgency, from a real deadline, but no threat and no trick.
choices: Some urgency, from a real deadline

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Upload your receipts in the app. No receipts or bank details go by email.
choices: Click a link and sign in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Open the HelvetiCare app yourself. The email says to.
choices: Click a link in the email

actions.label: Open the HelvetiCare app yourself and upload the receipts
actions.consequence: The upload works and your claim is on time.

actions.label: Make a note and upload them next week
actions.consequence: That is fine: the deadline is real, so just keep it in mind.

actions.label: Reply with the receipts attached
actions.consequence: The email said they never ask for receipts by email. Use the app.

attacker_reveal: This one is real, dear. It has a deadline, yet the domain is right, no link is given and it says what to do in the app. A deadline is not proof of a trap.
